Section 20 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act 1956 reads as under : "20. Maintenance of children and aged parents. (1) Subject to the provisions of this section a Hindu is bound, during his or her lifetime, to maintain his or her legitimate or illegitimate children and his or her aged or infirm parents. (2) A legitimate or illegitimate child may claim maintenance from his or her father or Kumari Radhika (Minor) Aged About 7 ... vs Shri Arun Kumar Sharma on 15 April, 2011 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140377794/ 7 mother so long as the child is a minor. (3) The obligation of a person to maintain his or her aged or infirm parent or a daughter who is unmarried extends in so far as the parent or the unmarried daughter, as the case may be, is unable Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi to maintain himself or herself out of his or her own earnings or other property. "Maintenance" has been defined u/s. 3(b) of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act 1956 as under : "3 Definitions - In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires (a) ...................................... (b) "Maintenance" includes (i) in all cases, provision for food, clothing, residence, education and medical attendance and treatment; (ii) in the case of an unmarried daughter, also the reasonable expenses of an incident to her marriage; (c) ............................................" A bare reading of section 20 suggest that the obligation to maintain the minor son, unmarried daughter, aged or infirm parents is personal and legal in character and arises from the very existence of relationship between the parties, independent and irrespective of the possession of property. So long as Ms. Radhika Kumari is in the custody of his mother Smt. Vibha Sharma which custody cannot in any way be said to be improper custody, it would be the duty of the father/defendant/respondent to provide for the maintenance of Ms. Radhika Kumari.(A. Annamalai Mudaliar Vs. Perumaves Ammal and others. Also Hon'ble Kerala High Court in case law reported as Viswambharan Vs. Dhanya and another AIR 2005 Kerala 91 (DB) has ruled as under : "19. Normally such liability to maintain would continue until the child attains the age of majority. Such liability to maintain the child, whatever be the sex, would continue until the child attains majority whether the child is or is not able to maintain itself out of its earnings or other property. So far as the male child is concerned, his right to claim maintenance would cease when he attains the age of majority. But so far as the female child is concerned, such right will continue even after she attains majority until she gets married provided she is unable to maintain herself out of her own earnings or other property." Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case law reported as Kishan Dutt Verma Vs. Baby Parul (Minor) and etc. AIR 2004 Delhi 366 has observed as under : "12. In Kirtikumer D. Vadodaria v. State of Gujarat (1996) 4 SCC 479 it was held in paragraph 8 of the Report : "According to the Law of the Land with regard to maintenance, there is an obligation of the husband Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi to maintain his wife which does not arise by reason of any contract - express or implied - but out of jural relationship of husband and wife consequent to the performance of marriage. Such as obligation of the husband to maintain his wife arises irrespective of the fact whether he has no property, as it is considered an imperative duty and a solemn obligation of the husband to maintain his wife. The husband cannot be heard saying that he is unable to maintain due to financial constraints so long as he is capable of earning. Further, according to Section 20 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, a Hindu is under a legal obligation to maintain his wife, minor sons, unmarried daughters and aged or infirm parents. The obligation to maintain them is personal, legal and absolute in character and arises from the very existence of the relationship between the parties." 13. Similarly, in State of Haryana Vs. Santra (2000) SC 1888) it was observed in paragraph 38 of the Report that parents are under an obligation to maintain their minor children. In paragraph 39 of the Report, it was held. "Maintenance would obviously include provision for food, clothing, residence, education of the children and medical attendance or treatment. The obligation to maintain besides being statutory in Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi nature is also personal in the sense that it arises from the very existence of the relationship between parent and the child. The obligation is absolute in terms and does not depend on the means of the father or the mother." 14. In view of the decisions of the Supreme Court, it must be held that the respondents are entitled to receive maintenances from the appellant." (1) It shall be in the discretion of the Court to determine whether any, and if so what, maintenance shall be awarded under the provisions of this Act, and in doing so, the court shall have due regard to the considerations set out in subsection (2), or sub section (3), as the case may be, so far as they are applicable. Further ld. counsel for plaintiff submitted that plaintiff was studying in third standard at the time of filing of suit & now she is studying in 12th standard & thus from the date of filing of affidavit Ex.P1 of Smt. Vibha Sharma, plaintiff is entitled to maintenance @ Rs.5,000/ p.m. It is submitted that now expenses are to be incurred on account of tution of plaintiff & her higher education. Written submission have also been filed on behalf of plaintiff. On the other hand, defendant has submitted that defendant had filed a petition u/s 9 Hindu Marriage Act which was later on withdrawn by defendant. It is submitted that maintenance was allowed to Smt. Vibha Sharma in those proceedings. Defendant further submitted that even today he is ready & willing to maintain the plaintiff & Smt. Vibha Sharma. It is vehemently submitted by defendant that Smt. Vibha Sharma has concealed her income. It is submitted that date of opening of Shiv Clinic is 3/04/1990 (i.e. prior to date of marriage of Smt. Vibha Sharma & defendant). It is submitted that property no. 189/13 Main Krishna Gali, Mauj Pur, Delhi is owned by daughter of Dr. C.S. Sharma. Further it is submitted that Ex. PW1/A is only a complaint & he fail to understand as to how Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi plaintiff/Smt. Vibha Sharma got copy of the same. It is submitted that clinic was closed on the complaint of Adarsh Mohalla Sudhar Samiti: It is submitted that defendant was not registered at Delhi & hence clinic was closed. Defendant has submitted that property no. 1456A Gali No.4 Shalimar Park, Shahdara Delhi is joint property owned by defendant and his brother Ravinder Kumar jointly & defendant has disposed of his share in the year 2002 in favour of Mr. Suraj Prakash Kaushik. Regarding the agricultural land at Village Bharawadh Distt. Baghpat (UP) defendant has submitted that copy of the fard has been obtained after forging his signature. It is submitted that land at Village Bharawadh is measuring only 18 Bighas & defendant has disposed of his share in the land & the sale proceeds have been spent in the treatment of mother of defendant who was suffering from cancer. It is submitted that maintenance u/s 125 Cr. PC has already been ordered. As per defendant, Smt. Vibha Sharma has not disclosed her present income. It is further submitted that Smt. Vibha Sharma has no brother and they are three sisters and after the death of her father she is having rental income from 9/10 rooms. Further defendant has submitted that plaintiff has not led any evidence to prove that defendant had beaten Smt. Vibha Sharma after taking liquor. Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi Defendant has vehemently argued that affidavit Ex. P1 is false & vital information about the income of Smt. Vibha Sharma has been concealed from the Court. Further stand of plaintiff/Smt. Vibha Sharma is that defendant is a man of means who is running his clinic.
texts.respondent_arguments: As per defendant, mother of plaintiff is shrewed lady having quarrelsome attitude and she on very first night of marriage disclosed to defendant that this marriage was solemnised against her wishes. Further defendant has alleged that mother of plaintiff has also concealed true facts of her monthly income and her service of a post graduate teacher who is M.A., B. Ed. Lastly, as per defendant mother of plaintiff is keeping and maintaining the plaintiff in a very decent manner right from her birth till today. 5. Plaintiff has filed replication to WS of defendant. In the replication, defence set up by defendant has been denied by plaintiff & the averments made in plaintiff have been reaffirmed. As per plaintiff, respondent turned her mother out of her matrimonial home after perpetuating cruelty on her and even when the mother of plaintiff tried to join and enter her matrimonial home, defendant did not allow her to enter the house. Further, as per plaintiff, plaintiff has been constrained to file the present suit only in order to save her own survival which has been threatened by the acts/commissions of the defendant. As alleged, plaintiff has a right to live with the dignity consistent with the human existence and being the daughter of defendant with the same status and dignity as of the defendant. The Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi rights of plaintiff, as submitted, to be brought up with dignity could not be snatched away under the garb of lame excuses or the flamboyant legal gargon. Plaintiff has denied the averment of defendant that Smt. Vibha Sharma is serving as a post graduate teacher. It has been reiterated in replication that mother of plaintiff has no income except the maintenance she is getting through Court under section 125 Cr.PC which is not sufficient to maintain the plaintiff as per living status and income of defendant/father. As per plaintiff,petition for restitution of conjugal rights filed by defendant was only an eye wash and was false and frivolous and the same was withdrawn by defendant out of fear when the cruelty of defendant became established before court. As alleged, defendant was never sincere to keep the mother of plaintiff with dignity and safety. As per plaintiff, defendant being biological father of plaintiff & defacto guardian of plaintiff is liable to provide the expenses for the maintenance including food, shelter and education etc. for the plaintiff. It is submitted that defendant has paid maintenance on two/three occasions and when defendant ceased to be capable of giving maintenance, defendant refused to pay the maintenance. Defendant has further submitted that maintenance can be ordered to be paid by defendant if and only if defendant otherwise refuses to maintain the plaintiff which he has not. It is submitted that Smt. Vibha Sharma is keeping the plaintiff with her of her own volition & otherwise he is ready & willing to maintain the both. Defendant has submitted that govt. bears the expenses of education of girl child. It is submitted that Smt. Vibha Sharma has not got registered the plaintiff under "Ladly" scheme. Defendant has further submitted that Smt. Vibha Sharma is Double M.A. & B. Ed. and she herself can teach the plaintiff & there is no need for any tutor. Defendant has submitted that the case of Smt. Vibha Sharma that she is maintaining plaintiff from borrowing/loans from other persons is not believe in as much as Smt. Vibha Sharma has not disclosed as to from where she borrowed the Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi money or took the loan. As per defendant liability to maintain plaintiff is joint liability of both the parents. Defendant has further submitted that electricity connection of his clinic has already been disconnected. Defendant in the course of arguments also referred to Ex. PW1/D. As per defendant, defendant has nothing and even for his survival he is dependant on other relatives & thus he cannot be made to pay maintenance. In rebuttal arguments, ld. counsel for plaintiff has submitted that no report has been filed by defendant regarding closure of his clinics. Further it is submitted that defendant has paid no amount to plaintiff/Smt. Vibha Sharma as regards maintenance. Further it is submitted that cheque of Rs.39,000/ given by defendant stood dishonourned & only a sum of Rs.3,000/ was paid by defendant. Further it is submitted that small payments of Rs.300/ & Rs.500/ etc. have also been made by defendant. Further it is submitted that Smt. Vibha Sharma did his LLB in 2001 & in the initial years of practice there is no income. It is submitted that in the property at Shalimar Park, Objectors were inducted as a tenant by defendant and they are ready to pay rent to defendant. 12. I have given a thoughtful consideration to the rival Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCum RC:East, Delhi submissions made by ld. counsel for plaintiff and the defendant in person keeping in view the facts and circumstances of this case as they arise on the basis of material available on judicial file. Also, as alleged, defendant is owning 50 Bighas of agricultural land at his native village vide Ex. PW1/B and Ex. PW1/C & is having income of Rs.1 lac per annum from the said land Respondent, as alleged, is earning Rs.40,000/ per month. In my opinion in the totality of facts and circumstances of this case, keeping in view the status and position of both Ms. Vibha Sharma, mother of plaintiff and Mr. Arun Kumar Sharma, father of plaintiff, the fact that plaintiff is receiving education from Govt. Pratibha Vikas Vidhyalaya, Yamuna Vihar, Delhi, reasonable wants of plaintiff it would be appropriate to order that defendant/respondent Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi Mr. Arun Kr. Sharma contributes a sum of Rs.2,000/ per month from the date of filing of this suit till the time plaintiff's attains majority & further even after plaintiff attaining majority till the time Ms. Radhika Kumari remains unmarried, if after attaining majority & before marriage, Ms. Radhika Kumari is unable to maintain herself out of his own earnings or other property.
texts.other_lawyer_arguments: Section 20 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act 1956 reads as under : "20. Maintenance of children and aged parents. (1) Subject to the provisions of this section a Hindu is bound, during his or her lifetime, to maintain his or her legitimate or illegitimate children and his or her aged or infirm parents. (2) A legitimate or illegitimate child may claim maintenance from his or her father or Kumari Radhika (Minor) Aged About 7 ... vs Shri Arun Kumar Sharma on 15 April, 2011 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140377794/ 7 mother so long as the child is a minor. (3) The obligation of a person to maintain his or her aged or infirm parent or a daughter who is unmarried extends in so far as the parent or the unmarried daughter, as the case may be, is unable Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi to maintain himself or herself out of his or her own earnings or other property. "Maintenance" has been defined u/s. 3(b) of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act 1956 as under : "3 Definitions - In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires (a) ...................................... (b) "Maintenance" includes (i) in all cases, provision for food, clothing, residence, education and medical attendance and treatment; (ii) in the case of an unmarried daughter, also the reasonable expenses of an incident to her marriage; (c) ............................................" A bare reading of section 20 suggest that the obligation to maintain the minor son, unmarried daughter, aged or infirm parents is personal and legal in character and arises from the very existence of relationship between the parties, independent and irrespective of the possession of property. So long as Ms. Radhika Kumari is in the custody of his mother Smt. Vibha Sharma which custody cannot in any way be said to be improper custody, it would be the duty of the father/defendant/respondent to provide for the maintenance of Ms. Radhika Kumari.(A. Annamalai Mudaliar Vs. Perumaves Ammal and others. Also Hon'ble Kerala High Court in case law reported as Viswambharan Vs. Dhanya and another AIR 2005 Kerala 91 (DB) has ruled as under : "19. It therefore follows that what Sec. 20 of Kumari Radhika (Minor) Aged About 7 ... vs Shri Arun Kumar Sharma on 15 April, 2011 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140377794/ 8 the Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi Act stipulates is that a Hindu parent is liable to maintain his legitimate or illegitimate male or female children. Normally such liability to maintain would continue until the child attains the age of majority. Such liability to maintain the child, whatever be the sex, would continue until the child attains majority whether the child is or is not able to maintain itself out of its earnings or other property. So far as the male child is concerned, his right to claim maintenance would cease when he attains the age of majority. But so far as the female child is concerned, such right will continue even after she attains majority until she gets married provided she is unable to maintain herself out of her own earnings or other property." Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case law reported as Kishan Dutt Verma Vs. Baby Parul (Minor) and etc. AIR 2004 Delhi 366 has observed as under : "12. In Kirtikumer D. Vadodaria v. State of Gujarat (1996) 4 SCC 479 it was held in paragraph 8 of the Report : "According to the Law of the Land with regard to maintenance, there is an obligation of the husband Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi to maintain his wife which does not arise by reason of any contract - express or implied - but out of jural relationship of husband and wife consequent to the performance of marriage. Such as obligation of the husband to maintain his wife arises irrespective of the fact whether he has no property, as it is considered an imperative duty and a solemn obligation of the husband to maintain his wife. The husband cannot be heard saying that he is unable to maintain due to financial constraints so long as he is capable of earning. Further, according to Section 20 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, a Hindu is under a legal obligation to maintain his wife, minor sons, unmarried daughters and aged or infirm parents. The obligation to maintain them is personal, legal and absolute in character and arises from the very existence of the relationship between the parties." 13. Similarly, in State of Haryana Vs. Santra (2000) SC 1888) it was observed in paragraph 38 of the Report that parents are under an obligation to maintain their minor children. In paragraph 39 of the Report, it was held. "Maintenance would obviously include provision for food, clothing, residence, education of the children and medical attendance or treatment. The obligation to maintain besides being statutory in Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi nature is also personal in the sense that it arises from the very existence of the relationship between parent and the child. The obligation is absolute in terms and does not depend on the means of the father or the mother." 14. In view of the decisions of the Supreme Court, it must be held that the respondents are entitled to receive maintenances from the appellant." Section 23 of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act 1956 reads as under : "23. Amount of maintenance. (1) It shall be in the discretion of the Court to determine whether any, and if so what, maintenance shall be awarded under the provisions of this Act, and in doing so, the court shall have due regard to the considerations set out in subsection (2), or sub section (3), as the case may be, so far as they are applicable. (2) In determining the amount of maintenance, if any, to be awarded to a wife, children or aged or infirm parents under this Act, regard shall be had to (a) the position and status of the parties; (b) the reasonable wants of the claimant; (c) if the claimant is living separately, whether the claimant is justified in doing so; (d) the value of the claimant's property and any income derived from such property, or from the claimant's own earnings or from any other source; (e) the number of persons entitled to maintenance under this Act.
